3. Mr. M. Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that sub-section 6 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 makes no provision for making the statutory deposit before the final determination of claim of the co-applicant and, as such, the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order arbitrarily. 

 5. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before us petitioner's application under sub-section 4 of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 for being added as a co-applicant (co-pre-emptor) and the impugned order passed by the Subordinate Judge allowing the petitioner's application for being added as a co-applicant for pre-emption with a direction to make the statutory deposit promptly. 

 6. The learned Advocate for the petitioner placed before us the case of Bidhu Chandra Majumder vs Oli Mia, reported in 1 BCR 293 in support of his contention. In this case it has been held that the deposit under section 96(1) of the S.A.T Act, 1950 is mandatory before filing the pre-emption case whereas the deposit under section 96(4) is not so.
